title: Healthcare Assistant
description:
Role Overview

Affinity Staff is recruiting compassionate and reliable Healthcare Assistants (HCAs) to join our agency team, supporting an established care facility in Chelmsford, Essex.

As a temporary HCA working through Affinity Staff, you will play a vital role in providing high-quality personal care, dignity, and companionship to residents. You will enjoy complete control over your schedule while benefiting from our dedicated, round-the-clock support.

Key Responsibilities
- Assisting residents with daily personal care, dressing, hygiene, and mobility needs.
- Supporting meal times, nutrition monitoring, and encouraging hydration.
- Promoting dignity, independence, and person-centred care at all times.
- Maintaining accurate care records and daily fluid/food intake documentation.
- Collaborating with senior carers and nursing staff to ensure a safe, supportive environment.

- NVQ Level 2 in Health & Social Care (preferred but not essential).

title: Enabling Support Worker
description:
Enabling Support Worker

Location: Cranfield Court, Chelmsford

Salary: £13.32 per hour

Hours: 40 hours per week

Are you the candidate we are looking for? At Shaftesbury Cranfield Court we are recruiting for Enabling Support Workers.

We are looking for people with the passion, talent, skills and experience that all add up to a caring and community-minded workforce.

We believe that the people we support have the right to a full and flourishing life. They deserve the very best in delivery. Driven by our core values, Shaftesbury strives to be Open, Enabling, Inclusive and Courageous in all that we do.

Our disability services across adult care, children's care and education are all focused on inclusion and support. Committed to professional, flexible and personalised care, we are passionate about going the extra mile in providing opportunities for people to thrive and live well.

About the role

As an Enabling Support Worker it will be your role to provide support and encouragement, by taking direction from both the person supported and the person centred support plan.

You will be required to maintain accurate records while at work, in line with the service requirements. You may also be required to administer personal care and medication.

There will be a requirement to cover sleep in sessions. You will be paid an additional £60 per sleep in.

Cranfield Court offers a high level of support 24/7, with person-centred, responsive care for up to 20 adults with physical and intellectual disabilities. Our experienced team provide positive behaviour support to ensure that those in our care are enabled to live a flourishing life.

Benefits of working at Shaftesbury

At Shaftesbury, we know that our people are our greatest asset. We're proud to have some of the best and most committed staff in the sector - and we want to attract more people like you to work with Shaftesbury. We're now offering even more great benefits to reward the work of our wonderful staff in adult care:
- Great CQC, great reward. If your service is rated good or equivalent by CQCin all domains, all staff will receive a £30 gift voucher. If rated outstanding, all staff will receive a £50 gift voucher.
- We want to reward staff in a range of ways for their hard work. You can be nominated for a recognition letter from a member of the Executive Leadership Team and you may also be nominated to receive a gift voucher up to £50 for going above and beyond within your role.
- Excellent training package provided for all staff.
- Generous Annual Leave entitlement of 25 days + 8 days bank holiday for the first 5 years. Increasing to 28 days + 8 days bank holiday after 5 years.
- Pension Scheme.
- Access to our employee assistance program.

Shaftesbury is the disability charity that's committed to enabling children, young people and adults to live a life that adds up for them.

What makes life liveable is never down to just one thing - it's the sum of many things. From friendship to fun; from companionship to community; from a great chat to a challenge overcome, it all adds up - to Shaftesbury.

Through a wide range of disability care, special education, and rehabilitation services we promote inclusion and wellbeing for all. Together, we work to see people take part, contribute and be valued. We put the elements in place that all add up to connected lives.

Shaftesbury is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of vulnerable children and adults and expects all employees to share this commitment. All offers of employment are subject to an enhanced DBS/Access NI check.

Shaftesbury is committed to the Disability Confident Scheme and to equal opportunities therefore we welcome and encourage applications from everyone regardless of age, disability, gender, ethnicity, religion and sexual orientation.

title: Care Assistant
description:
Care Assistant - Days

About the role:

As a Care Assistant with Runwood Homes, you'll join a dedicated team united by a profound desire to positively impact the lives of our residents. We're seeking Care Assistants who are wholeheartedly devoted to supporting our residents in embracing life to the fullest, promoting independence within a kind and compassionate setting.

At Runwood Homes, our residents and Care Assistants engage in daily moments filled with joy, laughter, and purposeful activities that bring meaning to their lives. Your commitment to enhancing the well-being and happiness of those in our care is truly valued and appreciated. Together, we create a warm and welcoming environment where every moment counts.

Benefits of working with Runwood Homes:
- 28 days Paid Holiday
- Weekly Pay
- Pension Scheme
- Blue Light Card and access to various other discounts on travel, restaurants, days out and leisure
- Employee Assistance Scheme that is also available to immediate family members
- Comprehensive induction and ongoing training
- Free DBS Check and uniform
- Funding and support towards obtaining NVQs
- Opportunities to progress your career within the company
- Employee of the Month awards

About you:

We do not require our Care Assistants to have experience although it is beneficial. We are seeking individuals whose empathy and warm-hearted approach stand out. Successful Care Assistants will have a positive, can-do attitude and excellent communication skills. Each day will bring something new, making for a diverse yet incredibly rewarding role.

About Runwood Homes:

Established in 1987, Runwood Homes is a leading provider of residential care, dementia care, and nursing care services, with a portfolio of 55 homes across England. Our commitment to delivering personalised care is at the core of our mission, as we strive to celebrate the lives of each and every one of our residents.

At Runwood Homes, we prioritise the professional development of our staff by investing in comprehensive internal, external, and e-training programs at all levels. This dedication to continuous learning and growth ensures that our team is equipped to provide the highest quality of care to our residents.

As we look towards the future, our reputation for delivering innovative care for individuals living with dementia continues to flourish. We are dedicated to pushing the boundaries of care excellence and setting new standards in the industry.

All appointments are subject to safer recruitment requirements to ensure the safeguarding of adults. All positions will involve appropriate checks and clearances.

You can apply for this role by completing our short application form or by visiting the home where one of our team can help you.

We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive sufficient applications or successfully recruit a suitable candidate. Early application is therefore encouraged.

title: Male Residential Support Worker - Children's LD Home
description:
Male Residential Support Workers x 3, Children's Learning Disability Home, Waltham Abbey, Essex

13.50 per hour plus 60 per sleep-in Full-time, permanent Rota including days, evenings, weekends and sleep-ins

We're recruiting three experienced, resilient male Residential Support Workers for a well-established, Ofsted-registered children's home in Waltham Abbey supporting young people with learning disabilities and autism. You'll be a positive, consistent role model for young people who need adults they can trust, with structure, patience and the confidence to stay calm when things get tough.

What you'll do
- Provide day-to-day care, guidance and emotional support, helping young people build routine, confidence, communication and independence skills
- Act as a positive male role model, using de-escalation, positive behaviour support and relationship-based approaches to support behaviour that challenges
- Support personal care, health needs and medication in line with care plans
- Keep young people safe, following safeguarding procedures, care plans and risk assessments
- Support education, health appointments, activities and family contact
- Keep accurate daily logs and incident reports to Ofsted standards
- Work closely with the Registered Manager, social workers, schools and other professionals

What you'll need
- At least 12 months' experience in an Ofsted-registered children's residential home, ideally supporting young people with learning disabilities and/or autism (supported accommodation, adult care or school settings alone won't count)
- Level 3 Diploma in Residential Childcare, or willingness to complete it
- Physical and emotional resilience, with experience of de-escalation and positive behaviour support (PMVA, MAPA or Team Teach an advantage)
- The right to work in the UK. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship.
- Willingness to work a flexible rota including sleep-ins
- A full UK driving licence is highly desirable

What's on offer
- 13.50 per hour plus 60 per sleep-in
- Ongoing training and support with qualifications
- A supportive management team and a real chance to make a difference
- Enhanced DBS provided

This role is open to male applicants only. Being male is an occupational requirement for this post under Schedule 9, Part 1 of the Equality Act 2010, to meet the needs of the young people currently living in the home.

Apply today with your CV. Shortlisted candidates will be contacted within 48 hours.

Night shift workers: 42 hours per week

At Bear Care, we believe every child deserves to feel safe, understood and supported to build a positive future.

We care for children who may have experienced trauma, disrupted relationships and significant challenges in their lives. Our aim is to provide a safe, stable and nurturing environment where children can build trust, develop emotional resilience and make progress at their own pace.

We are looking for warm, approachable and emotionally mature people who genuinely want to make a difference. Previous residential childcare experience is valuable, but it is not essential for the right candidate.

What we offer

We want our employees to feel supported, valued and able to develop throughout their career. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:
- Salary increase upon successfully completing your probation period
- A further salary increase once you achieve your relevant qualification
- Annual leave that increases with length of service
- Complimentary Perkbox membership, giving access to a range of discounts, rewards and wellbeing benefits
- Complimentary access to counselling services
- Long service awards
- Refer a friend bonus
- Funded CPD and ongoing learning opportunities
- Career development and progression opportunities
- A supportive working environment
- Boost your earnings by up to £5,200 per year through additional sleep-in shifts.

About the role

As a Residential Support Worker, you will:
- Provide emotional and social support, helping children and young people build positive and meaningful relationships.
- Support day-to-day routines including waking, mealtimes, school or college, activities and bedtime.
- Encourage participation in hobbies, activities and the local community.
- Build trusted and consistent relationships as a key worker for allocated children.
- Put our Therapeutic Framework into practice through your everyday interactions and support.
- Support children and young people to develop age-appropriate independence and life skills.
- Prepare meals and contribute to cooking, cleaning, shopping and laundry within the home.
- Promote the safety, welfare and wellbeing of children and young people at all times.
- Contribute to care plans, risk assessments and reviews, and maintain accurate records.

What we are looking for

We are looking for someone who:
- Has a genuine motivation and desire to improve the lives of children and young people.
- Has good communication and teamworking skills.
- Is aged 21 or over.

It would be great if you also have
- A Level 3 Diploma in Residential Childcare or equivalent, or are currently working towards one.
- Previous experience working in a children's residential setting.
- An understanding of trauma-informed or therapeutic approaches to care.
- A full UK driving licence.

Why join us?

Working in residential childcare is about much more than providing care. It's about being a consistent, trusted adult in a child's life and helping them develop the skills, confidence and relationships they need to move forward.

If you are compassionate, resilient and passionate about making a difference to children and young people, we would love to hear from you.

title: Outreach Recovery Worker
description:
Outreach Recovery Worker

Location: Southend on Sea

Salary: £26,000 - £28,000 per annum (DOE)

About The Role

We are looking for a compassionate, resilient and proactive Outreach Worker to engage with people who are rough sleeping or begging, including those who may be reluctant to engage with services or have multiple and complex needs.

You will provide assertive and flexible street outreach, building trusting relationships and supporting individuals to access accommodation, healthcare, mental health and substance misuse services. Working collaboratively with statutory and voluntary partners, you will help people identify their strengths, make positive and sustainable changes, and move towards safer and more settled lifestyles.

The role involves working across a range of locations and times, including some unsociable hours and in challenging weather conditions. You will maintain accurate records, contribute to multi-agency meetings and case planning, and ensure individuals receive coordinated support tailored to their needs.

About you

We are looking for someone who understands the challenges faced by people who are rough sleeping, begging or experiencing multiple and complex needs.

You will have:
- Knowledge of at least one of the following: substance misuse, alcohol misuse or mental health.
- An understanding of safeguarding, supported housing and multi-agency working.
- Experience of working positively with statutory and voluntary agencies.
- The ability to build relationships with people who may be reluctant to engage or display challenging behaviour.
- Good communication, administration, recording and reporting skills.
- A strength-based, person-centred approach, with the ability to maintain appropriate professional boundaries.
- Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office.
- The flexibility to work across different locations and undertake unsociable hours when required.
- A commitment to equality, inclusion and anti-discriminatory practice.
- Experience of facilitating multi-agency meetings would be desirable.

This role is subject to an enhanced DBS check.

About Us

We are The Forward Trust, the social enterprise with charitable status that empowers people to break the often interlinked cycles of crime and addiction to move forward with their lives. For more than 25 years we have been working with people to build positive and productive lives, whatever their past. We believe that anyone is capable of lasting change. Our services have supported thousands of people to make positive changes and build productive lives with a job, family, friends and a sense of community.

We are committed to our cause and the work we carry out as a charity. Equally the wellbeing and the employees who work for us are also important. Joining us an employee, we will offer you the following benefits -
- Flexible working
- Training and development opportunities
- Simply Health Cashback Scheme (optional)
- Season Ticket Loan Scheme
- Cycle to work scheme
- Crisis Loan Scheme
- Electric Car Scheme
- 3 x Wellbeing Days (pro rata'd for part time employees)
- Access to Blue Light Card
- 25 days (rising to 30 with length of service) Annual Leave plus Bank Holidays
- Contributory Pension Scheme Employer matched contributions of up to 6% in the first two years service and up to 9% thereafter
- Death in Service Payment (2x annual salary)
- Critical Illness Insurance (subject to qualifying criteria)

Please note that we may close this vacancy early if we receive a high volume of suitable applications.

To Apply

If you feel you are a suitable candidate and would like to work for Forward Trust, please click apply to be redirected to our website to complete your application.

title: Care Assistant Nights
description:

As a Care Assistant you will be assisting with mealtimes, personal care and completing current and appropriate documentation which includes daily record keeping, charts and care plans. Experience in a care environment either in a care home, as a home care worker or caring for a loved one would be ideal, however if you have a caring and kind approach and the desire to work with older people become one of the Excelcare family.
